exposure: prenatal management (termination of pregnancy, intrauterine treatment)
timing of diagnosis (<20 weeks vs. >= 20 weeks of gestation)
specific intrauterine therapies (blood transfusion, thoraco-amniotic shunt)
outcome: perinatal outcome (intrauterine fetal death, early neonatal death, late neonatal death)
cohort: The study included 80 fetuses diagnosed with hydrops fetalis (HF) or referred to a single tertiary center between 2012 and 2021.
finding: Nonimmune hydrops fetalis (NIHF) was the main etiology, and while diagnosis before 20 weeks of gestation was associated with worse perinatal outcomes, intrauterine therapy, when indicated, improved the survival rate.
